title: Adding spatial lookups to RasterField interpolated the user-supplied band index from the lookup tuple straight into the PostGIS SQL template, so a non-integer band index injects SQL.

findings.explanation: In the getquoted() method, when handling rasters, the code returns a string with user-controlled data interpolated directly into SQL: "'%s'::raster" % self.ewkb. The self.ewkb is derived from to_pgraster(obj), which processes user-provided raster data. While the raster format may have some inherent structure, string interpolation without parameterized queries is a potential SQL injection vector if the raster representation contains single quotes or other SQL metacharacters.
findings.suggested_fix: Use parameterized query placeholders instead of string interpolation for the raster case. Ensure the raster data is properly escaped or use Binary adapter for rasters similar to geometry handling.

findings.explanation: In the check_raster method, template_params are modified by directly embedding function calls like 'ST_Polygon(%s)' via string formatting: template_params['lhs'] = 'ST_Polygon(%s)' % template_params['lhs']. While this appears to work with template parameters from the ORM, if template_params values can be influenced by user input without proper escaping, this could be an injection point.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure template_params values come from parameterized placeholders, not raw user input. Verify the ORM layer properly escapes these values before they reach check_raster().

findings.explanation: This diff modifies database adapter and query construction logic for spatial types. It does not introduce any endpoint, access control logic, or user-controlled resource fetch operations. The changes are internal ORM-level query builders without authorization checks needed at this layer.

This diff extends database operators and operations for raster support. It does not modify authorization checks, permission validation, or access control mechanisms. Authorization should be enforced at the Django ORM QuerySet/view layer, not at the database operations layer.
